summary: DOJ Civil Division "Fraud Statistics - Overview" (FY2025 edition, published January 2026) gives every fiscal year FY1987-FY2025 for new qui tam and non-qui tam matters, settlements and judgments (qui tam split intervened/declined) and relator share awards, overall and by client agency (HHS, DoD, other); recorded in full, plus cells revised from the FY2024 and FY2023 editions. Annual DOJ press releases FY2010-FY2025 add rounded headline figures. The reward rules (1863 half share, 1943 cut, 1986 15-25%/25-30%), 2009/2010 amendments, the Zafirov ruling (2024) and its reversal by the 11th Circuit (September 1, 2026), and eight large settlements with stated relator shares are documented from statutes, CRS, court records and DOJ releases.

program_rules.quote: The private parties, known as relators, were entitled to half of the penalty recovered and costs, if successful.
program_rules.notes: Act of March 2, 1863, ch. 67, 12 Stat. 696, sec. 6 (cited by CRS). A fixed half; original 1863 statute text not retrieved (loc.gov blocked scripted download).

program_rules.quote: The private parties, known as relators, were entitled to half of the penalty recovered and costs, if successful.

program_rules.applies_to: government does not take over the case
program_rules.quote: it reduced the relator’s share of a successful suit from 50% to no more than 25% (no more than 10% should the government take up and litigate the case).
program_rules.notes: Public Law 78-213, 57 Stat. 608, approved December 23, 1943 (date from the U.S. Code historical notes to 3730: "restated Dec. 23, 1943, ch. 377, §1, 57 Stat. 608"). No statutory minimum.

program_rules.applies_to: government takes up and litigates the case

program_rules.notes: Unchanged in the current Code: 31 U.S.C. 3730(d)(1) (usa-uscode-31-3730-2023). Court may reduce the share of a relator who planned and initiated the violation (3730(d)(3)).

events.title: False Claims Act enacted (Civil War)
events.description: Act of March 2, 1863 (12 Stat. 696) let any person sue in the name of the United States to recover penalties for frauds on the government; the relator received half of the recovery.
events.quote: The False Claims Act originated as the Act of March 2, 1863.

events.title: 1943 amendments curtail qui tam
events.description: After the Attorney General sought repeal, Congress instead cut relator shares (max 25%, or 10% if the government took the case), required relators to hand over their evidence, gave the government 60 days to intervene, and barred suits based on information already in government hands (Pub. L. 78-213, 57 Stat. 608).
events.quote: The two Houses ultimately reached agreement and passed the compromise as Public Law 78-213.

events.title: False Claims Amendments Act of 1986
events.description: Pub. L. 99-562 revived qui tam: relator shares of 15-25% (government intervenes) or 25-30% (government declines), treble damages, higher penalties, anti-retaliation protection, and a new public-disclosure bar with an original-source exception. Qui tam filings rose from 31 new matters in FY1987 to hundreds a year.
events.quote: To amend title 31, United States Code, with respect to the fraudulent use of public property or money.

events.title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009 amends the FCA
events.description: FERA (Pub. L. 111-21, sec. 4) broadened FCA liability (no need for a claim to be presented directly to a federal officer, materiality defined, conspiracy and reverse false claims expanded) and rewrote the anti-retaliation provision 3730(h).
events.quote: The amendments of the Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009 reinforced the 1986 amendments

events.title: Affordable Care Act rewrites the public-disclosure bar
events.description: Pub. L. 111-148, sec. 10104(j)(2) replaced the jurisdictional public-disclosure bar with a dismissal rule the government can veto, limited qualifying disclosures to federal sources and the news media, and redefined "original source".
events.quote: 2010 —Subsec. (e)(4). Pub. L. 111–148 added par. (4) and struck out former par. (4)

events.title: Dodd-Frank adds 3-year limit for FCA retaliation claims
events.description: Pub. L. 111-203, sec. 1079A(c) amended 3730(h) (protection of "associated others" and an explicit 3-year limitations period for retaliation suits).
events.quote: Dodd-Frank added an explicit 3-year statute of limitations within which a civil action in response to retaliation must be commenced.

events.title: District court holds FCA qui tam unconstitutional (Zafirov)
events.description: Judge Mizelle (M.D. Fla.) held that relators are officers of the United States who are not appointed under Article II, so the qui tam provision violates the Appointments Clause; she dismissed Dr. Clarissa Zafirov's Medicare Advantage fraud suit (751 F. Supp. 3d 1293). The United States and the relator appealed (11th Cir. No. 24-13581).
events.quote: Because Zafirov initiated this FCA action when unconstitutionally appointed, I grant the defendants’ motion for judgment on the pleadings and dismiss the case.

events.title: Eleventh Circuit reverses Zafirov: qui tam does not violate the Appointments Clause
events.description: Published opinion (Branch, J.): relators do not occupy a continuing position established by law, so they are not officers; joins the 5th, 6th, 9th and 10th Circuits. District court order vacated and case remanded for the Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments, which remain open.
events.quote: we join our sister circuits that have addressed this issue and hold that the qui tam provisions of the FCA do not violate the Appointments Clause.

events.title: Record FCA year: over $6.8 billion and 1,297 qui tam suits in FY2025
events.description: DOJ reported the highest annual FCA settlements and judgments in the Act's history and a record number of qui tam filings (previous record 980 in FY2024).
events.quote: That amount is the highest in a single year in the history of the False Claims Act.

events.title: Relator trial verdict of $1.6 billion against Janssen (Penelow)
events.description: In a case the relators pursued, a jury returned a $1.6 billion verdict in U.S. ex rel. Penelow v. Janssen Products LP (Prezista and Intelence promotion); listed in DOJ's FY2025 fact sheet. Exact verdict date not given in the fact sheet.
events.quote: U.S. ex rel. Penelow v. Janssen Products LP, resulting in a $1.6 billion verdict

events.title: HCA settlement: largest combined qui tam award at the time ($151.6 million)
events.description: HCA paid $631 million in civil FCA damages and penalties; whistleblowers received a combined $151,591,500.
events.quote: the highest combined qui tam award ever paid out by the government.

programs.name: False Claims Act qui tam provisions (31 U.S.C. 3729-3733)
programs.notes: A private person (relator) files a False Claims Act suit on behalf of the United States, under seal. The Justice Department (Civil Division and U.S. Attorneys) investigates and decides whether to intervene; if it declines, the relator may pursue the case alone. A successful relator receives a share of the government's recovery set by statute: 15-25% if the government proceeds, 25-30% if it does not (since 1986). Originally enacted in 1863 (half of the recovery), cut back in 1943, revived by the 1986 amendments. Relator shares are paid out of the recovery, by court order or settlement. Constitutionality of qui tam challenged in Zafirov (M.D. Fla. 2024, vacated by the 11th Circuit on September 1, 2026). Statistics: DOJ Civil Division "Fraud Statistics - Overview", FY1987 onward.

new_indicators.name: Non-qui tam fraud matters opened
new_indicators.definition: New False Claims Act matters opened by the government itself (referrals and investigations not started by a whistleblower suit) in a period, as counted by the DOJ Civil Division ("New matters - non qui tam").
new_indicators.notes: Context for qui_tam_suits_filed: shows what share of new FCA matters come from whistleblowers.

new_indicators.name: Recoveries in cases not brought by whistleblowers
new_indicators.definition: Money recovered (settlements and judgments) in cases that did not originate in a whistleblower (qui tam) suit, in a period.
new_indicators.notes: DOJ FCA table column "Settlements and judgments - non qui tam". Has a series break at FY2020 (U.S. Attorneys' Office matters added).
